hypothesis: Consecutive-loss streak + tight-spread conditioned skip: skip the open leg of an oracle signal when EITHER (a) the last 2 consecutive closed positions both had negative estimated PnL (streak signal), OR (b) current spread > 1.1x rolling 60-tick median (spread signal). Reduce-only orders always execute. The streak captures serial correlation in adverse oracle regimes; the spread filter removes adverse entry moments where oracle reliability is lower.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, 12 trading days): streak-spread-tight $4772.0/106428 trades vs simple $1984.0/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+140.52%, well above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 37.1% vs 35.6% (+1.5pp). Max drawdown: -1.41% vs -3.77% (improved). Skip rate: 19.7% (26,108 fewer trades). Improvement consistent across ALL 12 dates. Config: sigma=5, seed=42, horizon=30s. Slippage: both 0.0 (zero fill-cost model, see research/NOTES.md).

hypothesis: Consecutive-loss streak AND spread-elevated conditioned skip: skip the open leg of an oracle signal only when BOTH (a) the last 2 consecutive closed positions had negative estimated PnL (streak signal) AND (b) current spread > 1.1x rolling 60-tick median (spread signal). One targeted change from streak-spread-tight: OR condition replaced with AND. All other parameters identical: spread_multiplier=1.1, spread_window=60, min_spread_window=10, streak_lookback=2. Hypothesis: the AND condition targets only the most adversarial regime (loss streak + elevated spread simultaneously) and reduces false-positive skips.
notes: PASS -- 12-date train window (20260308-20260320, 12 trading days): streak-spread-and $3007.0/128810 trades vs simple $1984.0/132536 trades; delta_pnl=+51.56%, above +5.0% gate. Win rate: 35.96% (weighted avg). Max drawdown: -2.68%. Skip rate: ~2.8% (3,726 fewer trades than baseline). AND condition fires much less often than OR (streak-spread-tight reduced trades by 19.7%; AND reduces by only 2.8%). Despite PASS, substantially underperforms streak-spread-tight ($3007 vs $4772, +51.56% vs +140.52%). Conclusion: individual OR signals (spread-alone, streak-alone) each have independent filtering power that AND discards. OR is the better architecture. Future iterations: tighten OR thresholds (spread_multiplier -> 1.05x, streak_lookback -> 3) or explore continuous score combining both signals.
